item.title: What changed for online sellers in 2026: the worries, the wins, and who it hits
item.description: Ten months in, the main fee you pay when something sells has stood still. Postage, parcels to Europe, eBay payouts and Etsy's photo rules are where 2026 moved. Here's what each change means for a small shop, in plain English.
item.content:encoded:
The short version: If you sell on Etsy, eBay or Mercari, the main fee you pay when something sells is the same today as it was in January. What moved this year is everything around the sale. USPS changed its prices four times, Europe added new charges on parcels, eBay changes how you get paid next week, and Etsy rewrote its photo rules.

None of it is a reason to panic. Most of it is a reason to spend one quiet evening checking your prices.

Find your shop first

Each row is one kind of shop, what changed for it, and the one thing to do, with the date it matters by.

If you...What changed for youDo this, by when
Sell physical items on EtsyOne unedited photo per listing; postage upAdd the photo to best sellers this week; reprice shipping before December
Sell patterns, recipes or other downloads on EtsyAI-written guides banned; a test lets buyers order printed copiesCheck your guides are your own work now; opt out of the print test if you'd rather
Resell on eBayPayout schedules may switch to on-demand from November 4After November 4, check your payout schedule in Seller Hub
Resell on MercariPrepaid label prices changed three timesRecheck what you charge on heavier items this week
Sell print on demandA 40-cent holiday surcharge on US ordersAdd it to shipping, or price it in, until January 17
Ship to buyers in the EU€3 duty since July; €2 handling fee from November 1Decide who pays before November 1
Sell less than $20,000 a yearYou usually won't get a 1099-K formKeep your records anyway

Who can ignore most of this: US shops that sell only downloads that aren't patterns or recipes. The postage and Europe changes don't touch you. Read your row, then skip to the good news.

The fees held still. The cost of getting a parcel there didn't.

Etsy's transaction fee is still 6.5% and a listing still costs 20 cents. Etsy revised its fee policy on October 5 without changing either one. eBay's and Mercari's main selling fees for US sellers haven't moved either.

So if you've been bracing for a fee hike, it hasn't come. The money went somewhere else: the label.

USPS raised its prices on January 18. On April 26 it added a temporary 8% on its main parcel services, which runs until January 17, 2027.

On July 12 it changed how some business label prices are worked out, including for parcels under a pound and for large, light boxes. Then, from October 4, a holiday increase landed on top, also until January 17.

Here's what that means for one order. Say a label cost you $6.00 last year, and you still charge $6.00 for shipping. The 8% on its own adds about 48 cents, before the January and holiday changes.

Etsy also takes 6.5% of what the buyer pays for shipping, which is 39 cents on $6.00. So that $6.00 charge now leaves you well short of what the label costs, and the gap comes out of your profit on every order.

That's the thing most sellers miss this year. The price list on the marketplace looks the same, so it feels like nothing changed. Your margin changed anyway. Etsy Basics walks through setting a shipping price that covers the label and the fee charged on it.

The worrying side

Four changes cost money, or catch people out if they don't know about them.

Mercari labels and print partners. Mercari's prepaid labels changed on January 20, again on May 7 to add the USPS surcharge, and again for some weights on October 19. Print partners Printful and Printify add 40 cents to each US order from October 15 to January 17.

Parcels to Europe. Since July 1 the EU has charged a €3 customs duty on low-value parcels from outside the EU. From November 1 it adds a €2 handling fee. Both are charged once for each different product in the parcel, not for each copy.

So a parcel with two identical mugs counts as one product: €3 of duty and €2 of handling. A parcel with a pen, a notebook and a key ring counts as three: €9 and €6. The handling fee isn't refunded if the buyer sends the parcel back. If you sell to EU buyers, decide before November 1 whether those charges go into your price or come out of your margin.

eBay payouts. eBay's new balance terms take effect for existing US sellers on November 4. Value Added Resource, which reported eBay's notice to sellers, says payout schedules switch to on-demand once a seller is enrolled. Daily, weekly and monthly payouts are still available. You just have to set yours again after November 4, or your money waits at eBay until you ask for it.

Etsy's photo and AI rules. Since October 22, most Etsy listings need at least one unedited photo of the real item on a real background. Print-on-demand items can use a stock mockup you're allowed to use, and downloads have their own rules. AI-written patterns and recipes are banned. The risk to watch: if a listing misses the rules and a buyer opens a case saying the item is different, Etsy may refund the buyer and you may be the one paying.

The good side

The $600 tax form isn't coming. For years, sellers were told that marketplaces and payment apps would send a Form 1099-K once sales passed $600. A 2025 law moved the line back to more than $20,000 and more than 200 sales in a year. A platform can still send one for less, and some states set lower limits. You owe tax on your profit either way.

Etsy is paying back more of its fee for the holidays. Until January 4, invited sellers in Etsy's Share & Save program get the full 6.5% transaction fee back on eligible sales that come through their own shared links. The usual refund is 4%.

Etsy's buyer protection got bigger. Since May 7, Etsy's Purchase Protection covers up to $250 of the refund on eligible orders of any size. Before, only orders of $250 or less were covered. That's a real help on the day a parcel goes missing.

What to do this week

  1. Reprice shipping against today's postage, not last year's.
  2. Shipping to the EU: decide before November 1 who pays the new charges.
  3. Etsy sellers: add one unedited photo to your best sellers, then work down the list.
  4. eBay sellers: after November 4, open Seller Hub, go to Payments, and set your payout schedule.
  5. In Share & Save? Share your links now, while the refund is the full 6.5%.

To see what one order really leaves you after Etsy's fees and your new postage, run it through our free fee calculator.

What we're still watching

Several seller guides report that TikTok Shop raised its US referral fee from 6% to 8% in August. TikTok's own public fee table still showed 6% when it was last checked, so we haven't counted it here. If you sell there, your settlement statement is the place to look.

Every fee change from here on gets its own short Fee Watch story, so you won't have to wait for a roundup. Earlier from the desk: this year's holiday shipping dates, and how to work out your own last order day.

What we checked: Etsy's fee, photo, Purchase Protection and Share & Save pages, USPS's own price announcements, Mercari's label page, the EU and Irish customs pages, eBay's new balance terms and the IRS 1099-K page. Most were read on October 27, 2026, and each one is listed below with its date.

item.title: Etsy's holiday shipping page still shows last year's dates. Here are this year's
item.description: Planning your Christmas cut-off from Etsy's help page? Its dates and surcharges still matched last December's when we checked, and two of them will cost you this year. Here's the real 2026 calendar, and how to find your own last order day.
item.content:encoded:
The short version: Etsy's help page for holiday shipping cut-offs still showed last December's dates when we checked it on October 22. For Priority Mail Express, that puts you a day late: Etsy says December 20, USPS says December 19. The page also understates the holiday postage rise. Below are this year's dates from the carriers themselves, and how to work out the last day a buyer can order from you.

It's the time of year when Etsy sellers start counting backwards from Christmas. Plenty of them will start where Etsy points them: a help page called "Understanding Shipping Carrier Surcharges & Cutoff Dates for the Holidays".

We read it on October 22 and compared it with a copy the Internet Archive saved on December 14, 2025. Every US date and surcharge note was the same, word for word. Christmas is still on the 25th. Several of the other numbers have moved.

Who can ignore this: shops that only sell digital downloads, and anyone who's already set their holiday cut-off from the carriers' own pages.

Two of last year's numbers will cost you

The Express date. Etsy's page says Priority Mail Express can go as late as December 20. This year USPS says December 19. If your buyer paid for Express so a gift arrives in time, the 20th is one day beyond USPS's recommended send-by date.

The postage rise. Etsy's page says Ground Advantage goes up "$.30-$.35" for the holidays. The real rise is bigger, and it has already started: USPS's holiday prices began on October 4 and run until January 17.

At USPS's commercial rates (its business prices for postage), a small parcel up to 3 lb now costs 40 cents more to nearby zones and 55 cents more to distant ones. Check what your own label service quotes.

That gap sounds small until you multiply it by a December's orders. And Etsy takes its 6.5% transaction fee on what buyers pay for shipping too (Etsy fees), so postage you don't pass on comes straight out of your margin.

The other differences mostly run the safe way. For UPS 3 Day Select and FedEx Express Saver, Etsy's page says December 19. Both carriers now say December 21, so Etsy's dates just cost you two selling days. Etsy's page says it will keep updating the list, so it may well change. Until it does, use the carriers' own dates.

This year's dates, from the carriers

USPS aims for delivery before Christmas Day. UPS and FedEx publish dates for delivery by Thursday, December 24. These are the dates to plan around, within the lower 48 states:

ServiceSend by
USPS Ground Advantage, First-Class MailThu, Dec 17
USPS Priority MailFri, Dec 18
USPS Priority Mail ExpressSat, Dec 19
UPS 3 Day Select / FedEx Express SaverMon, Dec 21
UPS 2nd Day Air / FedEx 2DayTue, Dec 22
UPS Next Day Air / FedEx OvernightWed, Dec 23
UPS Ground / FedEx GroundDepends on the route: Dec 17 for a 5-day FedEx route, later for shorter ones

Sources: USPS, UPS and FedEx. All three say their dates can change.

Shipping to Alaska or Hawaii? Priority and Express use the same dates. Ground Advantage has no date at all: USPS says to allow 10 days or more and to look up your exact ZIP codes. You'll see "December 16" quoted in some news reports. We couldn't find it on either USPS page.

Your real deadline is earlier than any of these

Here's the part most holiday guides skip. The carrier's date is when the parcel has to leave. The date that matters to your shop is the last day a buyer can order.

Etsy works out a buyer's delivery estimate as your processing time plus the carrier's transit time (Etsy Help). So count back from the carrier's date by your processing time. If your listings say 3 to 5 working days, count back 5. The table assumes you process orders Monday to Friday; if your shop also works weekends, your dates come a little later.

Your processing timeLast order day, Ground AdvantageLast order day, Priority Mail
1 working dayWed, Dec 16Thu, Dec 17
2 working daysTue, Dec 15Wed, Dec 16
3 working daysMon, Dec 14Tue, Dec 15
4 working daysFri, Dec 11Mon, Dec 14
5 working daysThu, Dec 10Fri, Dec 11

So a shop promising 5 working days by Ground Advantage should stop promising Christmas on December 10, a full week before the date on everyone's lips. These are planning dates, not a guarantee: parcels do run late in December, so leave a day spare.

Getting this right matters beyond Christmas. Etsy expects at least 80% of your orders to ship within the processing time you set, and shops that fall short can lose search visibility (Etsy Help). Choosing a processing time you can hit in your busiest week, as well as the quiet ones, is one of the first set-up decisions Etsy Basics walks you through.

What to do this week

  1. Write down your last order day from the table, using your longest processing time.
  2. Tell buyers. Put it in your shop announcement and an order-by line in your listings.
  3. Check your shipping price still covers the label. Pull one holiday postage quote for a typical order, then put it, and what you charge for shipping, into our free fee calculator for Etsy sellers. It shows what's left after postage and every Etsy fee.
  4. Shipping to Alaska or Hawaii by Ground Advantage? Look up the ZIP codes on USPS's delivery-time tool now.

We'll check Etsy's page again before December and update this story if it changes. Earlier from the desk: Etsy is quietly paying part of some buyers' shipping, and what it means for your fees.

What we checked: the USPS, UPS and FedEx holiday pages and price lists, Etsy's help pages, and the Internet Archive's copy of Etsy's page, all read on October 22, 2026. Every source is listed below.

Etsy Basics ($4.99), our seller guide, goes further on this, with dated sources. We publish and sell it.

item.title: Etsy is paying part of some US buyers' shipping. Your earnings and fees stay the same
item.description: Etsy is testing a cap on what some US buyers pay for calculated shipping, and covering the gap itself. Etsy has now confirmed your fees are still worked out on the full shipping amount, so nothing changes for you.
item.content:encoded:
Updated October 23, 2026: Etsy has answered the open question in our first version of this story. Fees are still charged on the full shipping amount, so there's no saving, and no loss, for you. We've rewritten the story around that answer.

The short version: Etsy is testing a cap on what some US buyers pay for calculated shipping, and Etsy pays the difference. Your item and shipping earnings stay the same, and so do your fees. You don't need to change anything.

Who can ignore this: shops that charge a fixed shipping price or offer free shipping. The test only touches orders that use calculated shipping.

What Etsy is doing

Etsy has emailed US sellers about a "limited, temporary, randomized" test. On some eligible orders that use calculated shipping, the buyer is charged a lower, capped shipping price, and Etsy covers the gap. The test is expected to run for a few weeks.

Etsy's own example, from the email as reproduced by Value Added Resource: your calculated shipping rate is $10, and the buyer is charged a capped $7.99.

You still receive the full $10. Etsy pays the other $2.01. Caps vary by order; $7.99 is the highest one Etsy is testing.

Your fees don't change either

When the test was first reported, nobody knew whether Etsy's fees would be charged on your full $10 or on the $7.99 the buyer paid. Etsy has now told Value Added Resource that transaction and payment-processing fees are still calculated on the full shipping amount, Etsy's share included.

So an order in the test looks exactly like a normal one from your side: same earnings, same fees. The only difference is that your buyer paid a little less for shipping, and Etsy made up the gap.

How you'll know an order was in the test

The difference shows as "Etsy-funded shipping" in that order's Order Details. Your Payment Account still shows your normal shipping revenue. Etsy says no listing or shipping-setting changes are needed. The reports don't say whether a shop can opt out.

Why Etsy is doing this

Etsy has said before that high shipping prices put buyers off. Since 2024 it has favored eligible US listings with shipping under $6 in search, but listings on calculated shipping were left out of that change, as Value Added Resource reported at the time.

This test looks like Etsy checking whether a cheaper shipping price brings more sales to calculated-shipping shops, with Etsy paying for it rather than you. Etsy says the results may inform future improvements to shipping. It hasn't said what those might be, and that's the part worth watching.

What to do

  1. Nothing to change. Keep your calculated shipping as it is.
  2. Watch your Order Details for "Etsy-funded shipping", so you know if your shop is in the test.
  3. Know your real take-home on a normal order. If shipping is a big part of your price, put one order into the free fee calculator for Etsy sellers. It shows what Etsy leaves you after every fee, shipping included.

We'll update this story if Etsy changes the test or says what comes next. Next from the desk: Etsy's holiday shipping page still shows last year's dates, with this year's from the carriers.

Etsy Basics ($4.99), our seller guide, goes further on this, with dated sources. We publish and sell it.
